mechanism_narrative: Residential mobility has increased monotonically from +10.3% to +24.3% over four weeks, indicating sustained confinement. As lockdown fatigue accumulates and restrictions remain static, suppressed retail demand will continue to decline further over the next four weeks due to habit formation around home-based consumption.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL increased every week from t-3w to t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC mean over next 28 days exceeds RETAIL_REC mean over last 28 days, or RESIDENTIAL mobility begins to decline week-on-week.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT mobility has collapsed to -73.6%, indicating near-total public transport shutdown. If transit remains below -70% for the next two weeks, retail recovery is mechanically blocked because essential workers and discretionary shoppers cannot reach retail locations, keeping RETAIL_REC depressed.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT remains below -70% for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: TRANSIT recovers above -60% within two weeks and RETAIL_REC simultaneously rises, or RETAIL_REC rises despite TRANSIT staying below -70%.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM and RETAIL_REC are both in severe decline (-22.1% and -50.1% respectively at t-0w). The divergence (grocery down 22 points, retail down 50 points) reflects prioritization of essential shopping. If this gap persists or widens, it signals behavioral substitution away from discretionary retail toward essential-only trips, sustaining retail depression.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM decline is less than 50% of RETAIL_REC decline for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC and GROCERY_PHARM converge to within 10 percentage points, or RETAIL_REC rises while GROCERY_PHARM remains stable or declines further.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility has collapsed from -26.4% to -42.6% over four weeks, indicating outdoor recreation is severely constrained. If parks remain below -40% for the next week, outdoor leisure substitution channels close, forcing consumers to remain home and further suppressing retail visits as alternative activities disappear.
candidate_trigger: PARKS falls below -40% in the next week
failure_condition: PARKS recovers above -35% within one week, or RETAIL_REC rises despite PARKS remaining below -40%.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES mobility has declined from -13.9% to -56.3% over four weeks, indicating near-total shift to remote work. This persistent workplace absence eliminates commute-based retail incidence and reduces weekday foot traffic. If WORKPLACES remains below -50% for the next four weeks, retail recovery is blocked by absence of workplace-anchored shopping patterns.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES remains below -50% for four consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES declined every week from -13.9% to -56.3%
failure_condition: WORKPLACES recovers above -40% within four weeks, or RETAIL_REC rises despite WORKPLACES staying below -50%.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT and WORKPLACES are both severely depressed (-73.6% and -56.3% respectively). The joint collapse of commuting infrastructure and workplace presence creates a dual barrier: no transport to retail, no reason to commute past retail. Only if both recover simultaneously can retail footfall resume. If either remains collapsed, retail stays depressed.
candidate_trigger: both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES remain below -50% for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: Either TRANSIT or WORKPLACES recovers above -40% while the other remains below -50%, and RETAIL_REC rises, or both recover above -40% and RETAIL_REC does not rise.

mechanism_narrative: Mid-April in Madrid typically sees spring retail demand recovery. However, RETAIL_REC is at -50.1% and declining monotonically each week. Seasonal upward pressure from spring weather is being overwhelmed by lockdown restrictions. If restrictions do not ease within four weeks, seasonal recovery will be suppressed and RETAIL_REC will remain depressed despite normal seasonal drivers.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC declined every week from -22.7% to -50.1%
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises above -40% within four weeks despite no observable policy change, or seasonal recovery occurs without policy easing.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM has declined from +8.0% to -22.1% over four weeks, indicating even essential shopping is being suppressed by restrictions. If essential shopping continues to decline, it signals tightening enforcement or supply-side closures. This signals regime intensification that will further suppress discretionary retail. RETAIL_REC will remain depressed as long as essential shopping is declining.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM declines for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM declined from +8.0% to -22.1% over four weeks
failure_condition: GROCERY_PHARM stabilizes or recovers above -15% within two weeks, or RETAIL_REC rises despite GROCERY_PHARM continuing to decline.
